skill.name: gh-cli
skill.description: GitHub CLI reference for using gh commands to manage repositories, issues, pull requests, Actions, projects, releases, gists, codespaces, organizations, and authentication.
skill.summary: Use GitHub CLI commands for common repository, collaboration, automation, and account workflows.
skill.author: github

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and GitHub CLI reference examples. Confirmed risks are privileged installation commands, GitHub token handling, and an eval-based shell completion snippet. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Privileged installation commands are included in the reference.
remediation.suggestion: Move sudo-based Linux installation steps to a clearly marked manual setup section and require confirmation before running them.

remediation.issue: Credential examples print, export, or weaken storage for GitHub tokens.
remediation.suggestion: Add warnings, prefer interactive login, and avoid recommending token printing or insecure storage in automation examples.

remediation.issue: Shell integration uses eval on generated completion output.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to review generated completion scripts first or follow official shell-specific installation guidance.

remediation.issue: Batch examples can modify many issues or pull requests.
remediation.suggestion: Add a preview step before xargs-based close, label, or edit operations and state the target repository scope.

content.value_statement: GitHub work often spans repositories, issues, pull requests, releases, and automation. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical gh command guidance.
actual_capabilities: Lists gh commands for authentication, repositories, issues, pull requests, and releases.
Shows workflows for GitHub Actions runs, artifacts, secrets, variables, and environments.
Covers organization, project, label, milestone, SSH key, and GPG key management.
Includes examples for gists, codespaces, API calls, aliases, and shell completion.
Provides batch workflow examples using gh JSON output, jq filters, and shell pipelines.
limitations: It is a reference skill and does not verify repository permissions before commands run.
Some examples can change GitHub resources or local shell configuration.
Authentication examples require careful token handling outside shared logs and terminals.
Command behavior depends on the installed gh version and GitHub account scopes.

use_cases.title: Review Pull Requests Faster
use_cases.description: Use gh commands to inspect, checkout, review, merge, and monitor pull requests from a terminal workflow.

use_cases.title: Automate Release Tasks
use_cases.description: Create releases, upload assets, inspect workflow runs, and download artifacts with repeatable CLI steps.

use_cases.title: Administer Repository Settings
use_cases.description: Manage labels, milestones, secrets, variables, deploy keys, collaborators, and organization resources through gh.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Basic Command
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the gh command to view my current GitHub authentication status and explain what the output means.

prompt_templates.title: Open a Pull Request Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Give me a safe gh workflow to create, view, and update a pull request for my current branch.

prompt_templates.title: Manage Actions Runs
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me inspect recent GitHub Actions failures, watch a rerun, and download artifacts with gh commands.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Batch Repository Operation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a cautious gh-based plan to update labels across many issues, including a preview step before changes.

output_examples.input: I need to check who I am authenticated as before creating a pull request.
output_examples.output: The skill would suggest checking authentication status, then viewing the active account and hostname before any write operation.

output_examples.input: I need to close stale issues with a comment.
output_examples.output: The skill would outline a search, preview matching issue numbers, and then run a batch close command after confirmation.

output_examples.input: I need release notes and assets for a new version.
output_examples.output: The skill would guide release creation, note generation, asset upload, and verification through GitHub CLI commands.

best_practices: Run read-only gh commands first to confirm repository, account, and target resources.
Use explicit owner and repository flags when working outside the current directory.
Keep tokens out of shell history, shared terminals, logs, and generated transcripts.
anti_patterns: Do not run sudo installation commands without reviewing the package source first.
Do not paste active GitHub tokens into prompts, issue comments, terminals, or logs.
Do not run batch update commands before previewing the affected issues or pull requests.

faq.question: Does this skill install GitHub CLI for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides installation commands, but the user or agent must decide whether to run them.

faq.question: Can it create or merge pull requests?
faq.answer: It can guide gh commands for those tasks when your account has the required repository permissions.

faq.question: Does it need a GitHub token?
faq.answer: Many write operations require authentication. Use the least privileged token or interactive login where possible.

faq.question: Can it manage GitHub Actions?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers listing runs, watching runs, rerunning jobs, downloading artifacts, and managing secrets or variables.

faq.question: Is it safe for production repositories?
faq.answer: Use caution. Many commands can change repository state, so preview targets and confirm permissions before writes.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
